newsitem.title: UK: Newcastle Utd plans UK stock market flotation.
newsitem.headline: Newcastle Utd plans UK stock market flotation.

text.p: English Premier League soccer club Newcastle United on Thursday confirmed plans for a UK stock market flotation.
The club said it plans to build a new football stadium with a 55,000-capacity and to convert its existing St James' Park ground into an indoor commercial leisure and sports centre.
In response to continued press speculation, Newcastle confirmed its intention to seek a listing for its shares on the London Stock Exchange in the spring of 1997.
"We intend to seek a stock market listing to assist in the financing of the next phase of the company's growth," joint chief executive Mark Corbridge said in a statement.
"Further details of the transaction will be made available in mid-January in line with the marketing timetable for the share issue," he added.
The club said that it would submit detailed plans to the city council for a new 65-million-stg purpose-built stadium.

Newcastle said both the new stadium and the St James' Park facility would be enclosed in an expanded and upgraded parkland area of 55 acres, a significant increase on the existing Leazes Park area of 35 acres.
Environmentalists have voiced concern over plans to build on park land in the north-east city.
Newcastle director Russell Jones said the project would provide a world class stadium and a larger urban park for the benefit of the community.

"NUFC's current rate of development exceeds that of any other football club in Europe and the planning application represents the first phase of the great sporting vision for the city of Newcastle," he said.
